about: Every mutant was applied to the file as it is at base_commit, which the change that adds this record does not change: it adds only tests, to the test module of the file's own tests (agent_import_split_journal_tests.rs). killer is the first test nextest reported failing (it stops at the first failure, with tests running in parallel, so another failing test may be reported first on another run). killer_at says where that test function exists: base, or this_commit for a test the change that adds this record adds. A test that exists at base may still kill only through cases that change adds to it: before_this_change gives the verdict at base where it differs. Each mutant that survived its filtered run at base was run again at base against every bridge test (the whole_set run, with no filter and nextest's --no-fail-fast, the approval stand-in example built) before it was called a survivor. Every survivor left at this_commit is listed in accepted_survivors with its reason: an equivalent one is marked equivalent. A hand-written mutant's mutation id is the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its edits in order, each as its from text, a NUL byte, its to text and a NUL byte, in UTF-8. Each edit's from text occurs exactly once in the file at base_commit, and applied_to names the file it was applied to. A tool mutant is named as cargo-mutants --list names it, by line and column. A mutant whose edit does not compile is recorded as unviable with the compiler's reason, not as caught. The file guards Microsoft Store package copies of the data folder, which exist on Windows only. Every run was made on macOS, where the tests stand in for Windows through the test-only task-local LOCAL_APP_DATA (what admit reads as %LOCALAPPDATA%) and the layout helper, which lays out a package copy in a temporary folder; the Windows native job does not run mutants. The hand-written mutants (J01 to J85) change, one at a time: in refused_message, the two messages swapped between the arms, the test on the cause (no cause taking the could-not-tell message, negated, always true, always false) and each of the three causes in NOT_TOLD_CAUSES; the two message constants each made empty and each made the other's; in SplitJournal::cause, each of the five strings changed, and the strings of OwnNotLocated and CopyNotLocated swapped; in the From impl for ToolFailure, the code empty, the cause left out and the cause empty; the refusal code IMPORT_JOURNAL_SPLIT changed; in admit, the scripted %LOCALAPPDATA% never read (the test arm), the host's %LOCALAPPDATA% never asked for (the or_else dropped), the early return for no %LOCALAPPDATA% giving NoOtherJournal, and the resolver giving nothing, giving the path as spelt for an existing file (no canonicalize), and giving a path for a file that does not exist; in admit_at, the early return for a folder outside %LOCALAPPDATA% (NoOtherJournal, a refusal), packages not listed (NoOtherJournal, another refusal), the copies found dropped, the path of this side's journal (the folder itself), this side's journal never located, own.is_none() (as is_some(), always true, always false), the NotFound match (!=, every error taken as no journal, a not-a-directory error also taken, a permission-denied error also taken, the refusing arm emptied, the two arms swapped, the refusal given as OtherNotRead or CopyNotLocated), the loop over the copies (the first not examined, only the first examined, the last not examined, reversed), the copy's journal looked for at the copy folder or never located, the test of a copy being this side's own (&& as ||, each half alone, == as !=, is_some() as is_none(), and the continue dropped), unlocated (&& as ||, each half alone, negated, own.is_none(), located.is_some()), the journal read at the journal file's path, and the match arms (an absent journal refused, batches == 0 as !=, <= 1, > 0 and == 1, the guard dropped, the unlocated arm's cause as OtherNotRead, OtherHoldsBatches or OwnNotLocated, its guard negated, always true, always false, the arm deleted, moved after the Read arm, before the Absent arm, before the no-batch arm and after the NotRead arm, a journal with batches refused as OtherNotRead, an unreadable one as OtherHoldsBatches), and the final answer given as NotRedirected. Not mutated: the derive lists, the items' visibility, the doc comments, the test module's attribute and path, the wording of the two messages (no test asserts wording; the messages are mutated as a whole, to empty and to each other, and the tool replaces refused_message by "" and "xyzzy"), the order of the strings in NOT_TOLD_CAUSES, the 100 ms pause in the closure handed to read_journal (it changes nothing a test can read but elapsed time; the retry it separates is read_journal_at's, in another file), and the arm of admit marked #[cfg(not(test))] (let scripted = None), which is compiled out of every test build, so no test can reach it and no mutant of it was run; every edit above is one change, so none of the lists above is every possible change to the line it names. Nineteen edits (J14, J15, J17, J19, J26, J31, J32, J37, J38, J41, J42, J44, J45, J51, J54, J62, J67, J82 and J85) were changed to an equivalent edit of the same kind (a neighbouring spelling of the same change: another replacement string for a cause, String::from("") for String::new(), Option::from(None) for None, the arm written in a block, || true and !true for true and false, the operands of || written the other way round, the same arm written with a block or a trailing comma, copy.as_path() for &copy, own == located for located == own, De Morgan's form of the negation, 0 != settlement.batches for the guard), because the first spelling gave a mutation id holding a run of eight or more decimal digits, which the privacy scan refuses; J26 needed a third spelling. J24 and J33 were first written without a type the compiler could infer (scripted alone; Vec::new()) and recorded as unviable; they were respelled (scripted.or(None::<PathBuf>); Vec::<PathBuf>::new()) and run again at base. In every run the file was byte for byte as at base_commit, checked after each restore (and, for the tool, after the run); the restore was a copy, never a rename. In the tool, hand and whole_set runs the test modules were as at base_commit; in survivors_again they are as this change leaves them.

runs.command: cargo mutants --in-place -p bridge --file src/agent_import_split_journal.rs --test-tool nextest --cargo-arg=--locked --timeout 900 --no-shuffle -- -E 'test(/agent::agent_import::split_journal::/) | test(/agent::agent_import::post::e2e_tests::/) | test(/agent::agent_import::desktop_journal_tests::/) | test(/agent::agent_import::tests::/)'

each mutant's edits applied as exact text, then cargo nextest run --locked -p bridge -E 'test(/agent::agent_import::split_journal::/) | test(/agent::agent_import::post::e2e_tests::/) | test(/agent::agent_import::desktop_journal_tests::/) | test(/agent::agent_import::tests::/)'

as the hand run with every bridge test (cargo nextest run --locked -p bridge --no-fail-fast -E 'all()'), for the 17 hand-written mutants the filtered run missed (the tool's run had no mutant missed); the unmutated baseline passed all 4923
as the hand run with -E 'test(/agent::agent_import::split_journal::/)', for the 17 hand-written mutants that survived the whole_set run
